A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TMEM163, as a novel zinc transporter, is critical for the maintenance of intracellular zinc levels in DGs and LEs.

BLOC1 is required for trafficking TMEM163 from the trans-Golgi network to the putative DG precursor compartments, and loss of TMEM 163 function results in DG defects and abnormal zinc accumulation in platelet granules.

BLOC-2 and AP-3 are required for trafficking TMEM163 from the Golgi apparatus to the perinuclear DG, whereas BLOC-1 and dysbindin are required for the trafficking and retention of TMEM163 within the perinuclear LE.
